skill.name: ai-crawler-readiness
skill.description: Verify that AI crawlers and assistants can actually reach and read a site, audit one page against the current public checks, and prove what changed since the last scan: re-run a full audit of the same URL with compareTo for added, resolved and persisting findings plus the score delta. Checks cover robots.txt per bot (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot), sitemap.xml, llms.txt, MCP discovery and agent readiness. Use when the question is AI visibility, bot blocking, llms.txt, sitemap, MCP discovery or agent access — or whether a fix actually worked. No API key.
skill.summary: Check public AI crawler access, audit page discovery signals, and compare findings before and after a site change.
skill.author: visdenda

security_audit.summary: The backtick and reconnaissance alerts describe Markdown tool references, public crawler policy, and audit comparisons, not shell execution or local system discovery. The operational endpoints send inputs to Visdenda, and the skill lacks explicit authorization checks for live probes and redaction guidance for log data. No evidence of embedded prompt injection or deliberate credential theft was found.

remediation.issue: Live checks accept a user-supplied target without explicit authorization guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Require authorization for live checks and restrict requests, redirects, and discovered links to approved public targets. Do not attempt to bypass access controls.

remediation.issue: Log-matching guidance does not specify what to redact before contacting Visdenda.
remediation.suggestion: Extract only the user-agent string, and send a source IP only for an approved verification. Do not send raw logs, cookies, or credentials.

remediation.issue: The skill does not disclose outbound data handling before starting a live audit or account handoff.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the provider, inputs, report access, and retention before an audit. Obtain separate consent before sending an account email or connecting a scoped key.

content.user_title: Audit AI Crawler Access and Site Readiness
content.value_statement: A valid robots.txt file does not tell you whether a specific crawler can reach your page. Check your public site and compare findings after a fix.
actual_capabilities: Identify the robots.txt rule that applies to a named crawler and path.
Check sitemap XML, declared sitemap links, and llms.txt structure.
Review canonical URLs, noindex directives, hreflang, and structured data on one page.
Review public MCP and OAuth discovery documents and agent cards.
Compare full audits of the same URL and report new, resolved, and remaining findings alongside the score change.
limitations: The audit covers one page and does not verify rankings, indexing, traffic, or citations.
Live checks require a client with Streamable HTTP support and send inputs to Visdenda.
The free service applies rate limits per IP and does not provide ongoing monitoring or Search Console data.
Only full audits can be compared, and the baseline must cover the same URL.

use_cases.title: Review a crawler policy change
use_cases.description: Confirm whether the rule for a named crawler matches your policy before reopening a public page.

use_cases.title: Validate a page after launch
use_cases.description: Check canonical and noindex signals on a public landing page and compare the result with an earlier full audit.

use_cases.title: Review public agent discovery
use_cases.description: Check that your MCP service publishes the intended discovery documents and distinguish missing optional files from broken configurations.

prompt_templates.title: Check a crawler rule
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review the crawler policy on a page you manage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether GPTBot is allowed by robots.txt for my public page at [URL]. Report the deciding rule and path without running a live page probe.

prompt_templates.title: Review sitemap and page signals
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Look for configuration errors after a page launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the sitemap and page signals for my public page at [URL]. Separate sitemap errors from canonical and noindex findings. Recommend one fix.

prompt_templates.title: Review MCP discovery documents
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Verify discovery documents for a service you operate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the public MCP and OAuth discovery documents for my service at [URL]. Separate broken references from optional files that are absent.

prompt_templates.title: Compare audits after a fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Measure changes against a full audit of the same page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full audit of my public page at [URL] and compare it with [previous scan ID]. Report new, resolved, and remaining findings, plus the score change.

output_examples.input: Check GPTBot policy for the public documentation page I manage.
output: Policy: GPTBot is disallowed on the documentation path.
Evidence: The crawler-specific rule applies to this path.
Scope: This result describes robots.txt policy, not how the page responds to a request.

output_examples.input: Compare the full audit after I fixed the sitemap declaration.
output: Resolved: The sitemap declaration now points to a valid XML sitemap.
Remaining: The page still declares a different canonical URL.
New findings: None. The readiness score rose from 72 to 81.

best_practices: Run live checks only on public targets you own or have permission to test.
Use a focused check for one issue and save full audits for before-and-after comparisons.
Review new and remaining findings before drawing conclusions from the score.
anti_patterns: Treating a favorable robots.txt rule as proof that a crawler can fetch the page.
Using a readiness score as evidence that an assistant cited the page.
Sending credentials, private URLs, or raw logs with a public check.

faq.question: Do public checks require an API key?
faq.answer: No. Public checks use the Visdenda endpoint without credentials. Account history and Search Console data require a separate connection.

faq.question: Can I compare two different page URLs?
faq.answer: No. You need a valid baseline from a full audit of the exact same URL.

faq.question: How long do full audit results remain available?
faq.answer: The report link lasts seven days. The service keeps the comparison baseline for 90 days.

faq.question: Does an allowed robots.txt rule prove a crawler can fetch the page?
faq.answer: No. The rule describes crawler policy. Authentication, a firewall, or another gate can still deny a request.

faq.question: Does a missing llms.txt file mean my site is broken?
faq.answer: No. The file is optional. Its absence only affects clients that look for it.

faq.question: Does a full audit crawl my whole website?
faq.answer: No. It audits one page and checks relevant site files. It does not perform a website-wide crawl.
